easy.title: Lion
easy.line: Large cat native to Africa and India

easy.text: The lion is a large cat of the genus Panthera.

easy.caption: Hybridisation between lion and snow leopard ancestors possibly continued until about 2.1 million years ago.

easy.text: Cultural depictions of lions have occurred worldwide, particularly as a symbol of power and royalty.

medium.title: Lion
medium.line: Large cat native to Africa and India

medium.text: The lion is a large cat of the genus Panthera, currently ranging only in Sub-Saharan Africa and India.

medium.caption: The Panthera lineage is estimated to have genetically diverged from the common ancestor of the Felidae around 10.8 million years ago.

events.label: Felis leo was the scientific name used by Carl Linnaeus in 1758.
The genus name Panthera was coined by Lorenz Oken in 1816.
Nevertheless, 17 births have been recorded in five prides between 2007 and 2015.
A 2025 study identified four stages in a roaring sequence: moaning, full-roaring, intermediary roaring.

medium.text: The lion inhabits grasslands, savannahs, and shrublands.
Cultural depictions of lions have occurred worldwide, particularly as a symbol of power and royalty.

The genus name Panthera was coined by Lorenz Oken in 1816.

deep.text: Between the mid-18th and mid-20th centuries, 26 lion specimens were described and proposed as subspecies, of which 11 were recognised as valid in 2005.
The lion is a muscular, broad-chested cat with a short, rounded head, a reduced neck, and round ears; males have broader heads.
The tuft is absent at birth, develops at around 5+1⁄2 months of age, and is readily identifiable at the age of seven months.
In the 19th and 20th centuries, several lion type specimens were described and proposed as subspecies, with about a dozen recognised as valid taxa until 2017.
The English word lion is derived via Anglo-Norman liun from Latin leōnem, which in turn was a borrowing from ancient Greek λέων léōn.
The fur varies in colour from light buff to silvery grey, yellowish red, and dark brown.
Cultural depictions of lions have occurred worldwide, particularly as a symbol of power and royalty.
